tests.name: Laboratory Accuracy Tests
tests.description: Tests intended for verifying compliance of the design and construction of a particular type or model of IR thermometer with the error limitations specified in 5.3 or 5.4.

tests.name: Blackbody Test
tests.description: Under laboratory conditions, an IR thermometer shall be tested against a blackbody standard using a procedure recommended by the manufacturer.

tests.name: Blackbody True Temperature Monitoring
tests.description: The true temperature of the blackbody shall be monitored by a contact imbedded or immersed thermometer with uncertainty no greater than ±0.03 °C (±0.05 °F).

tests.name: Ear Canal Type IR Thermometer Test
Skin Type IR Thermometer Test
tests.description: Testing as specified in 6.1.4 except blackbody temperatures set within ±1 °C (±2 °F) of 23, 30, and 38 °C (73, 86, and 100 °F).
tests.pass_criteria: Greatest calculated error δj from all data sets shall conform with requirements set forth in 5.4.

tests.name: Storage Test
tests.description: Test compliance with storage conditions.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests
tests.description: Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests - Purpose
tests.description: Clinical accuracy tests are intended for evaluation of accuracy of built-in instrumentational or combined site offsets, or both, and performance of an IR thermometer in assessing internal body temperatures from actual subjects.

tests.name: Clinical Accuracy Tests - Reference Sites
tests.description: Tests shall be performed on groups of subjects by using an internal body site (e.g., pulmonary artery or sublingual cavity) for reference measurements. IR thermometer shall be set in the corresponding mode.

tests.name: Shock Test - Drop Procedure
tests.description: IR thermometer subjected to a fall from a height of 1 m (39 in.) onto a 50 mm (2 in.) thick hardwood board (density > 700 kg/m3) lying flat on a rigid base (concrete block). Performed with controlled orientation once for each of two axes (Axis A: optical axis of probe; Axis B: through center of gravity and point where probe window crosses Axis A), with IR thermometer probe facing down.

tests.name: Shock Test - Post-Drop Measurement
tests.description: IR thermometer operation tested by measuring temperature of a blackbody set within ±0.5°C (±1°F) from 37°C (98.6°F), at ambient temperature 20-26°C (68-79°F) and relative humidity 40-70%. At least five measurements performed using a new disposable probe cover (if applicable) for every measurement. IR thermometer set in unadjusted mode as specified in 5.8.2.2.

tests.name: Shock Test - Error Evaluation
tests.description: Unadjusted temperature value subtracted from blackbody setting. Absolute value of largest error shall be no greater than error limit in 5.3 (or 5.4, whichever applicable) for blackbody temperature range 36-39°C (96.8-102.2°F).

tests.name: EMC - Radiofrequency Field Exposure
tests.description: Instrument exposed to modulated electromagnetic radiofrequency field in accordance with IEC601-1-2 and IEC 1000-4-3.

tests.name: EMC - Field Strength
tests.description: 3 V/m

tests.name: EMC - Carrier Frequency Range
tests.description: 26 MHz to 1 GHz

tests.name: EMC - Frequency Sweep Interval
tests.description: 1 MHz/s minimum

tests.name: EMC - Frequency Interval Dwell Time
tests.description: The greater of either 1 s or the measurement response time of the instrument under test.

tests.name: EMC - AM Modulation
tests.description: AM modulation, 80% index with a sine wave or 100% with a square wave having 50% duty cycle. Modulation frequency within each significant signal-processing passband of instrument. For devices without defined passband, modulation shall be 1 Hz, 10 Hz, and 1 kHz.

tests.name: EMC - Probe Cover Requirement
tests.description: No change of probe covers required while performing the electromagnetic compatibility test.

tests.name: EMC - Target Requirement
tests.description: IR thermometer probe shall be aimed at a target whose surface temperature is within the display range of the IR thermometer. Target does not have to be a blackbody.

tests.name: EMC - Continuous Reading Comparison
tests.description: IR thermometers capable of producing continuous temperature readings shall have their readings taken successively and compared to one another during the frequency sweep interval.

tests.name: Electrostatic Discharge Tests
conditions: IR thermometer shall be in power on state
Ten air and ten contact discharges shall be applied
If no exposed electrically conductive parts, only air discharge applied

sub_tests.name: Air Discharge
sub_tests.target: Electrically nonconductive part of the IR thermometer probe with no probe cover attached

sub_tests.name: Contact Discharge
sub_tests.target: Electrically conductive parts on the device

tests.post_test: Test according to procedures of 6.3.2 and 6.3.3 after ESD

tests.name: Accuracy Determination
tests.description: A manufacturer shall make available upon request specific instructions for tests to determine the laboratory error, clinical bias, and clinical repeatability of an IR thermometer. When describing how clinical tests are performed, the manufacturer shall disclose the profile of subject groups tested, including age and febrile status. A detailed procedure for taking reference temperatures also shall be disclosed.

semantic_fragments.content: All the requirements of ASTM E 1965-98(2016) were evaluated in this test report except the following clauses: 5.5.1 Clinical Accuracy is not evaluated in this report. 5.9.1 Housing Materials is not evaluated in this report. 6.2 Clinical Accuracy Tests. Condition of acceptability: 1) 5.5.1 Clinical Accuracy is not evaluated in this report. 2) 5.9.1 Housing Materials is not evaluated in this report. 3) 6.2 Clinical Accuracy Tests.

The test results presented in this report relate only to the object tested. Without permission of the Report department this test report is not permitted to be duplicated in extracts. This report shall not be reproduced except in full without the written approval of the testing laboratory. List of test equipment must be kept on file and available for review.

Possible test case verdicts: N/A - test case does not apply to the test object; Pass (P) - test object does meet the requirement; N/E - test object was not evaluated for the requirement. Throughout this report a comma/point is used as the decimal separator. '(see Attachment #)' refers to additional information appended to the report. '(see appended table)' refers to a table appended to the report.
The artwork below may be only a draft. The use of certification marks on a product must be authorized by the respective NCBs that own these marks.

Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report. Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used. Any disclosure of clinical accuracy claims shall be accompanied by disclosure of methodology and procedures. Clinical accuracy should be determined in the form of two characteristics — clinical bias with stated uncertainty and clinical repeatability.

The device under test has no ear canal mode (5.2.1, 5.3, 5.3.1.1, 5.3.1.2 are all N/A). The device operates as a skin/forehead IR thermometer only, with a display range of 32°C ~ 43°C in forehead (FA) mode.

The operating temperature range of the device is 10°C - 40°C, which is narrower than the standard-specified range of 16 to 40°C for the laboratory error test but meets the requirement that the upper limit shall not be less than 35°C. Because the range is narrower than the standard specification of 5.6.1.1, clause 5.6.1.2 applies and the device shall be clearly labeled with cautionary statements regarding operating temperature limits.

Storage Conditions: The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements after having been stored or transported at any point in an environment of –20 to +50°C and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. Results recorded in TABLE 5.6.4 with verdict P (Pass).
Electromagnetic Immunity requirement (5.6.6) is not applicable because the device is not intended for professional use.
Probe cover requirements (5.9.2, 5.9.2.1, 5.9.2.2, 5.9.2.3, 5.10.2, 5.10.2.1) are all not applicable because no probe cover is used with this device.
Housing Materials biocompatibility (5.9.1) is marked N/E (Not Evaluated in this report); evidence is provided via a separate Biocompatibility test report provided by the manufacturer.

Labeling requirement 5.10.1.3 regarding adjusted/unadjusted mode labeling on the instrument housing is not applicable for this device because it is intended for non-professional use and displays only one mode. However, the instruction manual must still specify body site(s) used to reference adjusted temperature values.

Sampling plans: Each producer or distributor who represents its instruments as conforming to this specification shall utilize statistically based sampling plans that are appropriate for each particular manufacturing process, in the design qualification of the device, and shall keep such essential records as are necessary to document with a high degree of assurance its claims that all of the requirements of this specification are met. The manufacturer shall make the sampling plans available upon request.

Ear Canal type IR thermometer test procedure (6.1.4.1–6.1.4.7): Tests shall be repeated for three blackbody temperatures (35, 37, 41 °C) within ±0.5 °C. Prior to measurements, thermometer shall be stabilized for minimum 30 min. At each combination of operating temperature and humidity, at least six measurements shall be taken per blackbody temperature. A new disposable probe cover must be used for each test reading. In each mode, three data sets shall be formed by pooling δj values across ambient conditions. The greatest δj is a measure of laboratory error. Correction method for unadjusted temperature from adjusted mode readings shall follow manufacturer's recommendation. All these clauses are marked N/A because this device has no ear type mode.

Clinical Accuracy Tests (6.2): This specification does not prescribe an actual method for determining clinical accuracy or establish specifications for values which characterize clinical accuracy. Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. An example of a method which may be used for this purpose is provided in X2.3. Result: N/E (Not Evaluated).

Clinical accuracy tests are intended for evaluation of accuracy of built-in instrumentational or combined site offsets, or both, and performance of an IR thermometer in assessing internal body temperatures from actual subjects. While this specification does not set limits for clinical accuracy, it is the responsibility of a manufacturer to determine values characterizing clinical accuracy and disclose them upon request.

Shock Test drop procedure: IR thermometer subjected to a fall from 1 m onto a 50 mm thick hardwood board (density > 700 kg/m3) on a rigid base. Two axes tested with probe facing down. Axis A is the optical axis of the probe. Axis B passes through the IR thermometer center of gravity and the point where the window of the probe crosses axis A.

Post-shock accuracy verification: Blackbody set within ±0.5°C from 37°C; ambient 20-26°C; RH 40-70%; minimum 5 measurements with new disposable probe cover per measurement; unadjusted mode per 5.8.2.2. Largest absolute error must not exceed limit in 5.3 or 5.4 for 36-39°C blackbody temperature range.

Electromagnetic Susceptibility Test (6.4) and all sub-clauses (6.4.1 through 6.4.2.3) are marked N/A for this product. The test requires exposure to modulated radiofrequency field (3 V/m, 26 MHz to 1 GHz, per IEC601-1-2 and IEC 1000-4-3) with specific conditions including no probe cover change, aiming at in-range target, and successive reading comparison during frequency sweep.

In order that purchasers may identify products conforming to requirements of this specification, producers and distributors may include a statement of compliance in conjunction with their name and address on product labels or associated printed materials, or both, such as invoices, sales literature, and the like. The following statement is suggested: 'This infrared thermometer meets requirements established in ASTM Standard (E1965-98). Full responsibility for the conformance of this product to the standard is assumed by (name and address of producer or distributor).' In the event one or more provisions of this standard are not met, a cautionary statement shall be included.

An instruction manual shall be provided and contain the system specifications including, but not limited to: displayed temperature range, maximum laboratory error, body site(s) used as a reference for adjusting the displayed temperature value, and applicable subject categories for each display mode. Response references 'Product performance' section of the User's Manual.

Non-conductive and dielectric connections (for example, fiber-optic) shall be used between the IR thermometer and all test equipment so as to minimize perturbations of the electromagnetic field. (Clause 6.4.2.6, Status: N/A)

The instruction manual shall inform the user of differences in the accuracy of measurements obtained with IR thermometers versus contact thermometers (that is, mercury-in-glass and electronic thermometers). Such differences shall include, whenever applicable, a description of the anticipated error sources associated with disposable or reusable probe covers and sleeves, operators' technique, anatomical variations, earwax buildups, subject cooperation, etc. In addition, this section of the instruction manual that explains differences in the accuracy of measurements obtained with IR thermometers versus contact thermometers shall conspicuously include the following statement: 'ASTM laboratory accuracy requirements in the display range of 37 to 39 °C (98 to 102 °F) for IR thermometers is ± 0.2 °C (±0.4 °F), whereas for mercury-in-glass and electronic thermometers, the requirement per ASTM Standards E667-86 and E1112-86 is ± 0.1 °C (±0.2 °F).'

The instruction manual shall specify whether the probe cover is intended for single use or multiple use. If multiple use is allowed, cleaning instructions and criteria for determining when a probe cover should be discarded shall be specified. Cleaning instructions shall be adequate to prevent cross-contamination between patients.

Detailed instructions—The instruction manual shall contain adequate instructions for use with sufficient detail for training in the operation, application, care, and biological and physical cleaning of the instrument and accessories. The instruction manual shall include warnings if performance of the instrument may be adversely affected should one or more of the following occur: operation outside subject temperature range, operating temperature and humidity range, storage temperature and humidity range, mechanical shock, soiled or damaged infrared optical components.
Keywords (Clause 8): auditory canal; body temperature; ear; fever; infrared; medical instrument; temperature; thermometer; tympanic

Operating Temperature Range Test (5.6.1) Supplementary Information: 1) Combination of the environmental temperature and humidity ranges: At each blackbody temperature, the tests shall be repeated under the ambient conditions stated in Table 1. 2) The individual measurement error is: δj = |tj - tBB| Where: tj = displayed or calculated value of unadjusted temperature, tBB = true temperature of the blackbody, j = sequential number of a reading, | | = signifies taking an absolute value. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

Shock Test (5.6.3) Supplementary Information: The individual measurement error is: δj = |tj - tBB| Where: tj = displayed or calculated value of unadjusted temperature, tBB = true temperature of the blackbody, j = sequential number of a reading, | | = signifies taking an absolute value. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

Clause 7.4 - Accuracy Determination: A manufacturer shall make available upon request specific instructions for tests to determine the laboratory error, clinical bias, and clinical repeatability of an IR thermometer. When describing how clinical tests are performed, the manufacturer shall disclose the profile of subject groups tested, including age and febrile status. A detailed procedure for taking reference temperatures also shall be disclosed. Reference: See 'Maintenance' of User's Manual.

Individual measurement error formula: δj = |tj - tBB|, where tj = displayed or calculated value of unadjusted temperature, tBB = true temperature of the blackbody, j = sequential number of a reading, | | = signifies taking an absolute value. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

requirements.description: The following requirements shall apply to any IR thermometer that is labeled to meet these specifications.
Displayed Temperature Range
In any display mode, an ear canal IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 34.4 to 42.2 °C (94.0 to 108.0 °F).
A skin IR thermometer shall display a subject's temperature over a minimum range of 22 to 40.0 °C (71.6 to 104.0 °F).
Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (for an Ear Canal IR Thermometer)
Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6), laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.4 shall be no greater than values specified below.
For blackbody temperature range from 36 to 39 °C (96.8 to 102.2 °F): 0.2 °C (0.4 °F).
For blackbody temperatures less than 36 °C (96.8 °F) or greater than 39 °C (102.2 °F): 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).
Maximum Permissible Laboratory Error (for a Skin IR Thermometer)

Within the manufacturer's specified operating ambient conditions (see 5.6) over the display temperature range as specified in 5.2.2, laboratory error δ as measured according to 6.1.5 shall be no greater than 0.3 °C (0.5 °F).
Special Requirements
Clinical Accuracy
The clinical accuracy requirement is applicable only to an ear canal IR thermometer system and the corresponding age groups of subjects for which such a thermometer is labeled or implied to be used.

Clinical accuracy shall be determined separately for each of the following conditions: for each device model, for each adjusted display mode, and for every age group of febrile and afebrile subjects on which the IR thermometer is intended to be used.
requirements.result_remark: Clinical accuracy is not evaluated in this report.

requirements.description: Any disclosure of clinical accuracy claims shall be accompanied by disclosure of methodology and procedures. Such information shall be made available on request.
Clinical accuracy should be determined in the form of two characteristics — clinical bias with stated uncertainty and clinical repeatability, as defined in 3.2.9.
Ambient Conditions
Operating Temperature Range
The system shall meet laboratory error requirements as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, when operating in an environment from 16 to 40 °C (60.8 to 104.0 °F).
If the operating temperature range is narrower than specified in 5.6.1.1, the device shall be clearly labeled with a cautionary statement of the maximum or minimum operating temperatures, or both.
Under no circumstances may the upper limit of operating temperature range be less than 35 °C (95 °F).
Operating Humidity Range — The relative humidity range for the operating temperature range as specified in 5.6.1 is up to 95%, noncondensing.
Shock

The instrument with batteries installed (if applicable) without a carrying (storage) casing shall withstand drops with controlled orientation of the device without degradation of accuracy as specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for a blackbody temperature of or near 37 °C (98.6 °F), when tested according to 6.3.
If an IR thermometer does not meet the requirement of 5.6.3.1, a means of detecting and informing the user of its inoperable state, after being subjected to shock, shall be provided.

Storage Conditions — The instrument shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, after having been stored or transported, or both, at any point in an environment of –20 to +50 °C (–4 to +122 °F) and relative humidity up to 95%, noncondensing, for a period of one month. The test procedure is specified in 6.1.6.
Cleaning and Disinfection—Instrument performance shall not be degraded by using the manufacturer's recommended procedures for cleaning and disinfection provided in the instruction manual.

Electromagnetic Immunity—An IR thermometer that is intended for professional use shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 or 5.4, or both, for temperature ranges of 6.3.2, during and after exposure to electromagnetic interference.
Electrostatic Discharge—An IR thermometer shall meet the accuracy requirements of 5.3 and 5.4, or both, for temperature ranges of 6.3.2, after 5 s after being subjected to electrostatic discharge.

Low Power Supply Operation—The instrument shall operate at power supply voltage lower by no less than 0.1 V than that required for indication of low power supply sign as specified by 5.8.3. The test of operation is defined in 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.
Display and Human Interface
Resolution—The resolution of a display shall be 0.1 °C (0.1 °F).
Modes
An IR thermometer shall indicate in what mode the instrument is set.
Unadjusted Mode—The unadjusted mode shall be accessible by the user either by setting the instrument into that mode directly or by a conversion technique from adjusted mode.
The adjusted mode sets an IR thermometer to represent a reference body site, such as core, oral, rectal, etc.

requirements.description: Warning Signs—The instrument shall have means to inform the operator when the following are outside the operating ranges specified by the manufacturer: power supply, subject temperature, and ambient temperature.

Housing Materials—All materials that may come in contact with the operator or a subject shall be nontoxic.

requirements.description: Probe Covers
To provide a sanitary barrier between a subject and the probe, a probe cover that comes in contact with a subject.
A probe and a probe cover of the system shall have shape and dimensions that prevent injury to a subject of any age.
A probe cover shall not increase laboratory errors whose limits are set in 5.3.1.
Labeling and Marking (Instruments and Accessories)
Thermometer and Accessories
A thermometer shall clearly indicate the units of its temperature scale.

requirements.description: An IR thermometer housing shall be clearly marked with the trade name or type of the device, or both, model designation, name of the manufacturer or distributor, and lot number or serial number.

An IR thermometer intended for professional use shall be conspicuously labelled with an indication of the unadjusted or adjusted mode(s), or both, that correspond to the temperature value(s) capable of being displayed by the instrument. Such labeling is optional for IR thermometers that display only one mode and are intended for non-professional use. However, the instruction manual for both professional and non-professional use IR thermometers shall specify the body site(s) used to reference the adjusted temperature value(s) displayed.
Probe Covers Package

The package shall state the name and type of the enclosed products, name of the manufacturer or distributor, lot number or serial number, and expiration date (if the probe covers have limited shelf life).
The thermometer model(s) for which the covers are intended for use shall be specified on the probe cover package.
The package shall state whether the probe cover is intended for single use or multiple use.

Any probe cover handling, application, storage, or cleaning procedures which impact the ability of an IR thermometer to meet the requirements for maximum permissible laboratory error specified in 5.3 shall be stated.

The tests are not required for every produced instrument. Each producer or distributor shall utilize statistically based sampling plans appropriate for each particular manufacturing process, in the design qualification of the device, and shall keep essential records necessary to document with a high degree of assurance its claims that all requirements of this specification are met.
The manufacturer shall make the sampling plans available upon request.
Laboratory Accuracy Tests

General—Laboratory accuracy tests are intended for verifying compliance of the design and construction of a particular type or model of IR thermometer with the error limitations specified in 5.3 or 5.4, or both.
Blackbody

Under laboratory conditions, an IR thermometer shall be tested against a blackbody standard. The temperature of a blackbody shall be measured by the IR thermometer being tested in accordance with a procedure recommended by the manufacturer for the particular IR thermometer.
The true temperature of the blackbody shall be monitored by a contact imbedded or immersed thermometer with uncertainty no greater than ±0.03 °C (±0.05 °F).
A manufacturer may require that an IR thermometer is tested only with a manufacturer-specified blackbody, rather than that described in Annex A1.
Ear Canal Type IR Thermometer

Tests shall be repeated for three blackbody temperatures set within ±0.5 °C (±1 °F) of the following temperatures: 35, 37, and 41 °C (95, 98.6, and 105.8 °F). At each blackbody temperature, the tests shall be repeated under the ambient conditions stated in Table 1.
Prior to the measurements, the IR thermometer shall be stabilized at given conditions of ambient temperature and humidity for a minimum of 30 min or longer if so specified by the manufacturer.

At each combination of operating temperature and humidity in Table 1, at least six measurements shall be taken for each blackbody temperature t_BB. The number of readings shall be the same for all combinations. A new disposable probe cover (if applicable) must be used for each test reading. The rate and method of temperature taking shall be in compliance with the manufacturer's recommendations.
The requirements of 5.3 demand that no individual error δj exceeds the specified limits for laboratory error.

In each mode, three data sets shall be formed. Each data set is comprised of values δj obtained at the same blackbody temperature setting by pooling together values for all combinations of operating temperature and humidities obtained at that blackbody temperature. The largest δj is a measure of the laboratory error of a system.

The correction method to arrive at unadjusted temperature tj from readings in adjusted mode(s) shall be used according to the manufacturer's recommendation. Such recommendations shall be available from the manufacturer on request and provided in the service and repair manual, if any (see 7.3).
To comply with this standard, the greatest calculated error δj from all data sets measured and calculated for all display modes shall conform with requirements set forth in 5.3.
Skin Type IR Thermometer
Testing is as specified in 6.1.4 except that blackbody temperatures shall be set within ±1 °C (±2 °F) from the following temperatures: 23, 30, and 38 °C (73, 86, and 100 °F).
The greatest calculated error δj from all data sets shall conform with requirements set forth in 5.4.

Storage Test—To test compliance with storage conditions, an IR thermometer shall be maintained in an environmental chamber at temperature –20 °C (–4 °F), relative humidity below 50%, for a period of 30 days and at 50 °C (122 °F), relative humidity no less than 75% noncondensing, for a period of 30 days. After each exposure the IR thermometer shall be tested according to 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.

Clinical Accuracy Tests—This specification does not prescribe an actual method for determining clinical accuracy or establish specifications for values which characterize clinical accuracy. Manufacturers shall perform clinical accuracy testing in accordance with methods acceptable to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.

IR thermometers not capable of producing continuous temperature readings shall have their circuitry modified to allow for continuous monitoring of the IR and reference temperature signals. The peak excursions of the monitored IR and reference temperature signals measured during frequency sweep interval shall be recalculated to represent the corresponding temperature excursions. On request, the manufacturer shall make available the method of the circuit modification.
IR thermometers having digital output shall have their signal monitored at the output of the analog-to-digital converter.
Non-conductive and dielectric connections (for example, fiber-optic) shall be used between the IR thermometer and all test equipment so as to minimize perturbations of the electromagnetic field.
Calculated temperature excursions shall deviate from one another by value no greater than required by 5.6.6.
Electrostatic Discharge Tests
The effects of electrostatic discharge on accuracy of an IR thermometer shall be tested in compliance with provisions of standard IEC 1000-4-2: 1995.
The IR thermometer shall be in a 'power on' state when subjected to electrostatic discharge.
Ten air and ten contact discharges shall be applied.
If IR thermometer under test has no exposed electrically conductive parts, only air discharge shall be applied.
Air Discharge
The discharge shall be aimed at an electrically nonconductive part of the IR thermometer probe with no probe cover attached.
The level of discharge shall be 2, 4, and 8 kV.
Contact Discharge
The probe of the electrostatic discharge device shall touch one of the electrically conductive parts on the device.
The level of discharge shall be 2, 4, and 6 kV.
After electrostatic discharge, the IR thermometer shall be tested according to the procedures of 6.3.2 and 6.3.3.
Documentation
Identification

In order that purchasers may identify products conforming to requirements of this specification, producers and distributors may include a statement of compliance in conjunction with their name and address on product labels or associated printed materials. Suggested statement: 'This infrared thermometer meets requirements established in ASTM Standard (E1965-98). Full responsibility for the conformance of this product to the standard is assumed by (name and address of producer or distributor).' In the event one or more provisions of this standard are not met, a cautionary statement shall be included.
The IR thermometer shall be identified as intended for professional or consumer use, or both, as applicable.
Instruction Manual

Specifications — An instruction manual shall be provided and contain the system specifications including, but not limited to: displayed temperature range, maximum laboratory error, body site(s) used as reference, applicable subject categories for each display mode.

requirements.description: Operation outside of the manufacturer-specified subject temperature range.
Operation outside of the manufacturer-specified operating temperature and humidity ranges.
Storage outside of the manufacturer-specified ambient temperature and humidity ranges.
Mechanical shock.
Manufacturer-defined soiled or damaged infrared optical components.
Absent, defective, or soiled probe cover (if applicable).
Use of unspecified probe covers.

Blackbody—The instruction manual shall indicate the type and availability of a blackbody recommended for verifying laboratory or clinical accuracy, or both, if only such type is required by the manufacturer as addressed in 6.1.3.3.

The instruction manual shall specify whether the probe cover is intended for single use or multiple use. If multiple use is allowed, cleaning instructions and criteria for determining when a probe cover should be discarded shall be specified. Cleaning instructions shall be adequate to prevent cross-contamination between patients.
The instruction manual shall inform the user of differences in the accuracy of measurements obtained with IR thermometers versus contact thermometers.
Service and Repair Manual
A detailed service manual shall be made available if user service or repair is permitted by the manufacturer.
A service manual shall disclose values of instrumentation or combined site offsets, or both.
A service manual shall provide a method of arriving at unadjusted readings from temperatures displayed in an adjusted mode.
